tilts.set: SET on 2026-11-06 by the Portfolio Fitness for Fighting judg

industry.why: Overweight, carried; the condition for Double Overweight (defensives leading for a second month with the industry's relative strength at B or better) is half met: defensives lead on all five windows, the three-month line at +6.6 points, but Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-11-06 against 2026-09-04, not week on week: C now, D prior, short of B. Component 1 regime, 6-Nov-26 (risk-off beneath an index at its high, now present in Europe's own prices: the STOXX Europe 600 0.9% from its 52-week high with the share of stocks above the 100, 150 and 200-day averages at or below the tenth percentile of near-high days since 2006, defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows, breadth recovering for a second week; the causes, inflation, rates, yields, credit and the consumer, unread this week because the strategist and newsletter files did not reach the pack, so the credit-and-cost-of-debt read of 30-Oct-26 with the US ten-year above 5% is held one week stale; sources present 2026-W45, headline-only). Three live holdings (Carlsberg 4.67%, Fevertree 2.48%, Hilton Food 4.78%, 11.93 points) read A on Thematic Fit/Momentum through this row. Counter-case: a defensive destination two months into a rotation is crowded, and no staples house view was read this week. To A if relative strength reaches B with defensives still leading at three months.

sector.why: Overweight, carried, on the special topic 'The UK Budget of 28-Oct-26': demand is defensive and the statutory pay floor rises 3.9% in April 2027 against 4.1% in April 2026, a small cost relief, with food tariffs cut; the market disagreed on the day (Sainsbury minus 2.5%, Kingfisher minus 2.6%). Component 1 regime, 30-Oct-26 (risk-off beneath a steady index, led now by credit and the cost of debt rather than by the artificial intelligence wash-out alone: the US ten-year above 5% after a hawkish Fed hold with two dissents for a hike, Goldman Sachs' Risk Appetite Indicator at its lowest since April 2025, euro investment-grade and high-yield yields up 30 and 90 basis points since September, Brent near $115, the French premium a record 150 basis points, Europe rotating to quality, defensives and non-AI growth, the STOXX Europe 600 1.7% from its high with breadth recovering from the bottom fifth of three years and defensives leading cyclicals at four weeks and three months; sources present 2026-W44): inflation sticky with energy pass-through is the regime that pays discount food retail (Danske Bank's call of 18 October stands). Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-30 against 2026-08-28, not week on week: C now, C prior. Three Pool names (Kesko, Distribuidora Internacional de Alimentacion, Greggs at the Bench cut). Not Double Overweight on one house and a Budget; counter-case: thin margins under cost inflation and a UK consumer with 2027 growth at 1.0%. To A if a second house names food retail or a European consumer reading arrives falling with volumes holding.

geography.why: Neutral, carried. No source spoke to Poland this week; Goldman's note (22 Oct) that emerging-market sovereign spreads are widening with US rate volatility is general, not Polish, and the condition for D (a source reading Polish spreads wider, or a third memo naming the sovereign) is not met; no memo carried a congruence line this week. Component 1 regime, 23-Oct-26 (risk-off confirmed and broadening: the discount-rate squeeze now a positioning wash-out in the artificial intelligence complex with credit leading it, bonds rallied as a hedge for the first time this cycle while the Fed still hikes in December, the US 10-year near 5.10%, Brent $111, French sovereign stress spilling into Italy, European defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows and breadth in the bottom fifth of three years; sources present 2026-W43). Twelve of the 149 Pool stocks are Polish, seven of them banks, so this is still the country row most likely to move. Relative strength is not graded by country.

defs.atr: average true range: each day's high to low, stretched to the previous close on a gap, as a % of the previous close; L5D the last 5 sessions, L1M and L3M the last 30 and 91 calendar days
defs.top_half: a close above the midpoint of the day's high-low range; an up day closes at or above the previous close; days with no range are left out
